A 30-Year Leader in Tight-Tolerance CNC Machining

J Smith Machine Works is a profitable, well-established precision machining business serving industrial, aerospace, and medical-device OEMs across the Pacific Northwest. Founded in 1994, it has grown into a trusted contract manufacturer known for tight-tolerance, complex components and long-tenured customer relationships.

Revenue is anchored by multi-year supply agreements with five blue-chip OEM customers, none representing more than 22% of sales. A seasoned operations team runs the floor day to day, and the owner has stepped back into a strategic role — positioning the business for a smooth ownership transition.

With a full order book, recent investment in five-axis capacity, and a fragmented supplier base ripe for consolidation, the business offers a strong platform for a strategic acquirer or an operator seeking an established, cash-generative manufacturer.

Capabilities & Equipment

5-Axis CNC machining

Recent investment in five-axis capacity for complex, tight-tolerance parts — with excess capacity to absorb new work.

ISO 9001:2015 certified

A documented quality system that creates high switching costs and qualifies the shop for regulated OEM programs.

In-house CMM inspection

Coordinate-measuring inspection and full traceability keep first-pass yield high and scrap low.

Lights-out automation

Pallet automation and bar-fed cells extend spindle hours well beyond a single shift.

Why it wins

Market Position

J Smith Machine Works sits in a durable niche: complex, low-to-mid-volume precision components for aerospace, defense, and medical-device OEMs concentrated in the Pacific Northwest industrial corridor. These programs demand certification, traceability, and proven reliability — barriers that protect incumbent suppliers and make switching costly.

With ISO 9001 certification, a 30-year track record, and a diversified blue-chip customer base, the business is well positioned to consolidate a fragmented local supplier market and win adjacent aerospace and medical work as it adds capacity.

At a glance

SWOT Analysis

Strengths

  • 30-year operating history
  • ISO 9001 certified
  • Diversified blue-chip customers (none >22%)
  • Recent five-axis investment

Weaknesses

  • Owner-linked key relationships
  • Skilled-labor market tightness
  • Peak-season capacity constraints

Opportunities

  • Excess five-axis capacity to grow into
  • Local supplier consolidation
  • Adjacent aerospace & medical programs

Threats

  • Raw-material cost swings
  • Customer reshoring / insourcing
  • Skilled-labor shortage
Room to run

Growth Plan

Add a second shift

Convert the current order-book backlog into revenue by extending machine hours across a second shift.

AS9100 certification

Unlock higher-margin aerospace programs by layering AS9100 onto the existing ISO 9001 system.

Automation cell expansion

Add pallet automation to raise spindle utilization and margins without proportional headcount.
